item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Minor grammatical quibble (emphasis mine):

SCP-323-1's metabolism will experience a dramatic increase, requiring a constant caloric intake, with starvation occurring anywhere between fifteen (15) to thirty (30) minutes if no self-preservation efforts are made.

The bolded section reads awkwardly for me. I feel like it should be 'with starvation occurring within fifteen (15) to thirty (30) minutes'; or if you want to keep the word 'between', it could be 'with starvation occurring anywhere between fifteen (15) to thirty (30) minutes later'.

Other than that, love your take on the wendigo! Upvoted.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Antlers coming out the sides of a skull is not anomalous, and therefore need not be specified. Their presence and size is sufficient. I thought it was one detail too many.

As for the rest, see below.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Err, it seems I got my own wires crossed while writing this. It's actually the placement of "unidentified" that's the problem.

The way it reads now suggests that this cervine skull is unidentified, i.e., we don't know if it belonged to Bob the Deer, Joe the Elk, or which specific cervid in particular. It should be rewritten to say that it is the skull of an unidentified cervid, thus necessitating the part of speech change.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I know nothing about cervidae, but grammatically, "cervine" serves as an adjective modifying the noun "skull". I see nothing wrong with that particular aspect of the phrasing.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Most female cervids don't have antlers. My opinion is the description is OK, because we need to know the size (and one or two antlers might be broken). Although the synthax makes it possible to imagine that it has a different pair of antlers growing from each side.

Maybe just say "the antlers measure…." and state the number of tines (points). And don't say from tip-to-tip because they have
many tips each.

That is a bit of nit-picking on my part, but what would make it an "identified" cervidae skull?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This has a bit of original series feel to it, but I'm not really liking it. Reading the whole thing, it doesn't seem to be just a thing what turns you into a psycho killer, at least, which made me downvote initially.

SCP-323 is a unidentified cervine skull measuring 55cm long, 27cm wide, and 31cm tall, with a pair of antlers, measuring 35cm tall and 46cm from tip to tip, growing from the left and right sides of SCP-323.

Antlers growing from the sides of a skull is not a detail that needs to be specified. It should be "the skull of an unidentified cervid", or possibly "species of cervid", 'cervine' being an adjectival form.
